Question: Which class of molecule is indicated by a mass spectrum with several intense peaks at a distance of 14 m/z?

Options:
A. Branched alkanes
B. Carboxylic acids
C. Phenol derivatives
D. n-alkanes

You MUST include the letter(s) of the correct answer (separated by comma if there are many) within the following tags: [ANSWER] and [/ANSWER].
For example, '[ANSWER]<answer>[/ANSWER]', where <answer> is comma- or space-separated list of the correct letters. Always answer in exactly this format of comma-separated letters between the two tags, even if you are unsure. We require this because we use automatic parsing.

Thought: In mass spectrometry, the pattern of peaks provides information about the structure of molecules. When there are several intense peaks separated by 14 m/z units, this typically indicates the sequential loss of CH2 groups (which have a mass of 14 atomic mass units). This pattern is characteristic of straight-chain hydrocarbons, specifically n-alkanes. 

The fragmentation pattern of n-alkanes shows regular peaks at intervals of 14 m/z because these molecules can break at different points along the carbon chain, each time losing a CH2 group. This creates a characteristic "fingerprint" pattern.

Branched alkanes (option A) would show a more complex fragmentation pattern due to preferential cleavage at branch points.
Carboxylic acids (option B) would show characteristic peaks related to the COOH group.
Phenol derivatives (option C) would show patterns related to the aromatic ring structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is D. n-alkanes.
